Modine Shares Gain Most in Six Years After Samsung Buyout Talks
items.d: Modine Manufacturing Co. logged its biggest single-day gain since 2020 after Bloomberg News reported the maker of cooling systems for data centers was in talks to be acquired by Samsung Electronics Co.

Send a tip to our reporters Site feedback: Take our Survey New Window Facebook X LinkedIn Email Link Gift By David Carnevali and Ryan Gould November 13, 2026 at 11:03 PM UTC Bookmark Save Takeaways by Bloomberg AI Modine Manufacturing Co. logged its biggest single-day gain since 2020 after Bloomberg News reported the maker of cooling systems for data centers was in talks to be acquired by Samsung Electronics Co. Shares of Racine, Wisconsin-based Modine closed 28% higher at $135.66 Friday in New York trading, elevating the company’s market value to $7.2 billion. The gains erased a 15% drop through Thursday since the company reported quarterly results Bloomberg Terminal last week that underwhelmed investors.

items.t: Morgan Stanley’s Shalett ‘Incredibly’ Bullish Despite AI Turmoil
items.d: Nvidia Corp.’s leadership turmoil and the Democrats’ midterm election victories have added to concerns about the artificial intelligence boom, but those won’t derail the main driver of the bull market: capital spending on AI infrastructure, says Morgan Stanley Wealth Management’s Lisa Shalett.
items.fullText: Technology Markets Morgan Stanley’s Shalett ‘Incredibly’ Bullish Despite AI Turmoil Facebook X LinkedIn Email Link Gift Facebook X LinkedIn Email Link Gift Gift this article Contact us: Provide news feedback or report an error Confidential tip? Send a tip to our reporters Site feedback: Take our Survey New Window Facebook X LinkedIn Email Link Gift By Natalia Kniazhevich November 13, 2026 at 10:22 PM UTC Bookmark Save Takeaways by Bloomberg AI Nvidia Corp.’s leadership turmoil and the Democrats’ midterm election victories have added to concerns about the artificial intelligence boom, but those won’t derail the main driver of the bull market: capital spending on AI infrastructure, says Morgan Stanley Wealth Management’s Lisa Shalett . The election results should not be viewed as a rejection of AI investment or data-center construction, she said. Instead, voters are demanding greater oversight of AI safety and a fairer distribution of the costs and benefits of data-center development. By focusing too heavily on political developments and volatility in technology stocks, investors are losing sight of the longer-term market narrative, said Shalett, CIO at Morgan Stanley Wealth Management, in an interview.

items.t: Blackstone’s QTS Is Cutting AI Debt Sale by More Than Half
items.d: QTS, a data center operator backed by Blackstone Inc., is slashing the size of a planned private debt sale by about 60% after struggling to attract enough demand from investors — and refusing to pay much higher yields.

Send a tip to our reporters Site feedback: Take our Survey New Window Facebook X LinkedIn Email Link Gift By Menghan Xiao and Emily Graffeo November 13, 2026 at 9:35 PM UTC Bookmark Save Takeaways by Bloomberg AI QTS , a data center operator backed by Blackstone Inc., is slashing the size of a planned private debt sale by about 60% after struggling to attract enough demand from investors — and refusing to pay much higher yields. The company is raising about $300 million after initially targeting roughly $800 million, according to people with knowledge of the transaction. Some investors balked at the price the borrower was offering, while some faced constraints because the company has tapped the private placement market several times, the people said, asking not to be identified discussing a private matter.

items.t: This young startup wants to power floating data centers with the ocean’s heat, and investors are already on board
items.d: Drogue is harvesting heat from the ocean to power data centers on floating vessels. The first prototype should be bobbing around the ocean, crunching bits, in less than two years.
items.fullText: Anyone who has weathered a hurricane can tell you that the oceans — which fuel the storms — contain a tremendous amount of energy. Thanks to global warming, they’re holding more than ever. A new startup wants to harness that energy to power data centers. Drogue , which has kept a low profile until now, is building a system that harvests heat from the ocean to power data centers on board floating vessels. According to founder and CEO Sam Sipe, the first prototype should be bobbing around the ocean, crunching bits, less than two years from now. The goal, Sipe said, is to help data center developers deploy servers in AI-friendly timelines. “The data center industry is a real estate game, and so they’re playing on 8- to 10-year timelines, including interoperability with utilities and [independent system operators]” that manage regional power grids, he said. “AI demand has increased 10x in just the last three years. It’s completely incompatible.” Drogue was founded just six months ago in Washington, D.C., and the startup told TechCrunch exclusively that it has already raised $20 million, including from XYZ Venture Capital, Toyota Ventures, Tamarack Global, Dream, FDVC, Garuda Ventures, Flexcap, Boost VC, and Slow Ventures, among other investors. In those six months, Drogue has designed a multi-megawatt prototype that will be installed on a traditional oceangoing ship and sent out to sea in early 2028. Future versions will be built on floating structures that more closely resemble offshore oil platforms. To Sipe, the decision to turn to the ocean was obvious. After years flying E-2D Hawkeyes off U.S. Navy aircraft carriers, he had an appreciation for the ocean’s immense power. “Most people think, oh, ocean — hard waves, storms, corrosion, biofouling. And I just see this majestic place and resource that we just ignore,” he said. An engineer operates a 3D printer at Drogue’s Washington, D.C., lab. items.t: The unfolding Jensen Huang scandal: a timeline
items.d: Jensen Huang has resigned from Nvidia following an affair, which could have ramifications for national security as the U.S. and China race to develop the most advanced AI infrastructure.
items.fullText: Nvidia co-founder and now former CEO Jensen Huang has never been as prone to controversy as AI leaders like OpenAI’s Sam Altman or SpaceXAI’s Elon Musk. But the 63-year-old industry kingpin recently admitted that he cheated on his wife of 40 years in affairs that could have ramifications beyond Huang’s personal life and U.S. national security. U.S. officials believe that one of Huang’s likely romantic interests, Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, is a Chinese spy who has been feeding information back to Beijing. (Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen, is of no relation to Jensen Huang.) Megaspeed is a Singapore-based AI infrastructure company that reportedly purchased $4.8 billion worth of Nvidia chips over the last two years. The U.S. and Singapore have both previously investigated Megaspeed over suspicions that the firm was illegally sharing chips with China. The Justice Department has since taken over the federal investigation into the company, The New York Times has reported. The story took a sudden turn on Wednesday. Citing five people who worked at Nvidia, the Times reported that Huang also had an extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell, the company’s vice president of healthcare, who reports directly to him. Nvidia, Huang and Powell have not confirmed the report. Reached by a Times reporter, Huang reportedly said, “I don’t think you should be talking to me directly,” before hanging up. By early Thursday morning, Huang was no longer CEO of the company he co-founded 33 years ago. Then, Thursday afternoon, Reuters dropped another bombshell, publishing a report alleging that Huang had yet another extramarital affair with another unnamed Nvidia employee. The U.S. and China are embroiled in a fierce technological arms race to build the most advanced AI infrastructure, which could shape each country’s economic future, military prowess, and capacity for innovation. items.fullText: 뉴스 한경 PREMIUM9 AI를 넘어서는 성공투자 구독하기 AI 추천 뉴스 AI 추천 뉴스 팝업 닫기 삼성, 美 데이터센터 냉각업체 인수 추진 입력 2026.11.13 17:37 수정 2026.11.14 01:40 지면 A10 기사 스크랩 기사 스크랩 댓글 댓글 기사 공유 공유 글자크기 조절 글자크기 프린트 프린트 노유정 기자 구독하기 구글 검색 선호 출처로 추가 Google 검색에서 한국경제 기사를 더 자주 볼 수 있습니다. M&A로 냉난방공조 승부수 시총 7.5조…하만 이후 최대규모 북미 영업망·생산거점 확보 기대 AI 인프라 전반 사업 확장 가속 삼성전자가 미국 데이터센터 냉각시스템 제조기업인 모딘매뉴팩처링 인수를 추진하는 것으로 알려졌다. 북미를 중심으로 인공지능(AI) 데이터센터가 늘어나며 서버의 열을 식히는 냉난방공조설비(HVAC) 수요가 급증하자 현지 시장 공략에 속도를 내기 위한 전략으로 풀이된다. 삼성전자는 최근 AI 모델 개발사부터 데이터센터 설비업체까지 투자 대상을 넓히며 지분 투자와 인수합병(M&A)에 나서고 있다. 급변하는 AI 생태계에서 주도권을 잡기 위해서는 기술력과 생산능력을 빠르게 확보해야 한다는 판단에서다. ◇“수주 내 인수 계약 가능성” 이미지 크게보기 지난 11일 블룸버그통신에 따르면 삼성전자와 모딘이 인수 협상을 하고 있으며, 이르면 수 주 안에 인수 계약이 성사될 것으로 전해졌다. 이에 대해 삼성전자 관계자는 “확인해줄 수 없다”고 했다. 모딘은 대형 상업용 건물과 산업용 장비에 쓰이는 냉난방 시스템을 생산하는 기업이다. 최근엔 AI 데이터센터용 냉난방공조 사업에 힘을 쏟고 있다. AI 데이터센터는 열을 많이 뿜어내는 서버가 대량 장착돼 있어 열 관리(공조)가 필수다. 모딘의 2027회계연도 1분기(4~6월) 매출은 8억7410만달러(약 1조1700억원)다. 이 중 데이터센터 부문 매출은 3억4860만달러로 전체의 약 40%를 차지한다. 데이터센터 부문 매출은 전년 같은 기간 대비 90% 증가했다. 북미 하이퍼스케일러를 고객사로 확보하며 매출이 큰 폭으로 늘었다. 모딘의 11일 종가 기준 시가총액은 56억달러(약 7조5000억원) 규모다. 지난 6월 기준 주요 주주는 글로벌 자산운용사 블랙록(7.24%), 뱅가드(5.20%)다. 삼성전자가 모딘 지분 100%를 인수한다면 2017년 80억달러(약 10조7000억원)에 하만을 인수한 이후 최대 규모 M&A가 될 전망이다. ◇AI 생태계 전방위 공략 HVAC는 삼성이 AI, 로봇 등과 함께 신성장동력으로 선정한 사업 분야다. 삼성전자는 지난해 독일 플랙트그룹을 15억유로(약 2조2000억원)에 인수하며 AI 데이터센터 등 대형 건물의 냉난방을 담당하는 ‘중앙 공조’ 사업에 본격 진출했다. 삼성전자는 인수 이후 생산능력을 적극적으로 늘리고 있다. 지난 8월 인도 푸네에서 플랙트그룹 신규 생산라인을 준공했다. 최근 국내 전남광주사업장에도 2400억원을 투자해 HVAC 생산라인을 구축하고 있다. 모딘 인수가 성사되면 삼성전자는 북미 영업망과 생산 거점을 추가로 확보하게 된다. 모딘은 텍사스와 버지니아 등 미국 주요 지역에 생산공장을 보유하고 있다. 이달부터는 텍사스주 신공장에서 데이터센터용 대형 냉각기 생산에 들어갔다. 모딘이 보유한 현지 고객사와의 협력 관계도 강점이다. 삼성은 올 들어 AI 생태계 전반으로 투자 범위를 넓히고 있다. 9월 프랑스 AI 기업 미스트랄AI에 수천억원을 투자해 AI 반도체 부문에서 협력하기로 했다. 같은 달 삼성전자와 삼성물산 등 6개 관계사는 미 AI 데이터센터 인프라 기업 헬릭스에도 10억달러를 투자했다. 업계 관계자는 “삼성이 고대역폭메모리(HBM)와 HVAC 등 데이터센터용 부품 공급을 넘어 AI 인프라 전반으로 사업 영역을 넓히려는 행보로 보인다”고 말했다. 노유정 기자 yjroh@hankyung.com 좋아요 싫어요 후속기사 원해요 ⓒ 한경닷컴, 무단전재 및 재배포 금지 한국경제 구독

items.t: "HBM 없는 AI 추론…열 빼기 쉬운 적층 구조가 해법"
items.fullText: 산업 한경 PREMIUM9 AI를 넘어서는 성공투자 구독하기 AI 추천 뉴스 AI 추천 뉴스 팝업 닫기 "HBM 없는 AI 추론…열 빼기 쉬운 적층 구조가 해법" 입력 2026.11.13 17:23 수정 2026.11.14 01:32 지면 A11 기사 스크랩 기사 스크랩 댓글 댓글 기사 공유 공유 글자크기 조절 글자크기 프린트 프린트 김인엽 기자 구독하기 구글 검색 선호 출처로 추가 Google 검색에서 한국경제 기사를 더 자주 볼 수 있습니다. 시드 세스 디매트릭스 CEO 삼전닉스 투자받은 美스타트업 메모리·연산 결합한 AI칩 개발 “앞으로 5년 간 가장 중요한 기술은 메모리와 연산장치를 함께 묶는 첨단 패키징입니다.” 시드 세스 디매트릭스(D-Matrix) 최고경영자(CEO·사진)는 지난 10일(현지시간) 미국 샌타클래라 본사에서 기자와 만나 이같이 말했다. 빅테크가 고대역폭메모리(HBM)를 모으는 사이 스타트업 디매트릭스는 전혀 다른 해법을 모색하고 있었다. HBM을 쓰지 않는 AI칩으로 추론 시장을 공략하겠다는 것이다. 2019년 설립된 디매트릭스는 추론(AI가 작업을 수행하는 과정)용 반도체를 개발하는 스타트업이다. 지난해 시리즈C 투자 유치 때 기업가치 20억달러(약 2조6700억원)를 인정받았다. SK하이닉스와 삼성벤처투자가 각각 시리즈A·B 투자에 참여했다. 세스 CEO는 “초기 투자자인 SK하이닉스는 장기적으로 추론에 새로운 메모리 구조가 필요하다는 문제의식에 공감했다”고 했다. 디매트릭스의 주력 제품은 추론용 칩 ‘커세어’다. 반도체 내 고속 메모리인 정적램(SRAM)을 중심으로 메모리와 연산부를 가깝게 배치해 데이터 이동시간과 전력효율을 높였다. 지난 9월에는 차세대 반도체인 ‘랩터’를 엔비디아의 네트워크 플랫폼 NV링크 퓨전과 MGX 랙에 통합하는 파트너십을 발표했다. 내년 4분기 출시를 목표로 개발 중인 ‘랩터’는 D램을 아래에, 연산장치를 위에 쌓는다. 연산장치 위에 메모리를 올리는 삼성전자의 ‘zHBM’과 위아래 배치가 반대다. 세스 CEO는 “연산장치가 위에 있으면 열을 빼내기 쉽다”며 “이미 확보한 패키징 기술을 활용해 제품을 더 빨리 내놓을 수 있다”고 설명했다. 세스 CEO는 미 중간선거 결과 데이터센터 건설이 지연되면 자사 반도체 가치가 더욱 높아질 것으로 봤다. 엔비디아 호퍼 등 구형 그래픽처리장치(GPU)에 자사 제품을 결합하면 성능을 1.5~2배 높이고 교체 시기를 늦출 수 있어서다. 실리콘밸리=김인엽 특파원 inside@hankyung.com 좋아요 싫어요 후속기사 원해요 ⓒ 한경닷컴, 무단전재 및 재배포 금지 한국경제 구독신청 한경 프리미엄9 구독신청 김인엽 특파원 한국경제신문 실리콘밸리 김인엽 특파원입니다. 정치부, 국제부를 거쳐 테크앤사이언스부에 있습니다. 현재 실리콘밸리 빅테크와 스타트업, 캘리포니아에서 일어나는 흥미로운 일들을 취재하고 있습니다. Nebius tests the neocloud playbook with $40 billion in planned spending
items.d: Nebius plans to fund its $40 billion AI infrastructure expansion through customer prepayments and loans, even as delays at a Microsoft data center raise questions about its financing model.
items.fullText: In its third-quarter earnings call Thursday, the neocloud company Nebius laid out $40 billion in planned spending for 2027, far more than Wall Street had expected. It’s an ambitious plan, but it rests on a string of planned projects that are already starting to show cracks. Nebius plans to fund the buildout by relying on customer pre-payments and loans backed by customer contracts — essentially using the future value of its data centers to finance their construction. But that can be a risky strategy if those projects get bogged down by delays or cancellations. “Building at this scale is hard, and delays are part of our industry right now,” CEO Arkady Volozh said during Thursday’s earnings call. “We are not immune.” The earnings announcement comes on the heels of reports that Microsoft is cooling on neocloud deals that aren’t delivering on time. That’s a problem for companies like Nebius, whose financing strategy is becoming more dependent on repayments. Because if it can’t get to capacity on time, it will keep piling on costs while revenues slip. One of Nebius’ largest customers is Microsoft, which is paying for AI computing capacity at a Vineland, New Jersey, data center that is now months behind schedule. Nebius’ contract with Microsoft is worth up to $19.4 billion, but it’s already letting deadlines slip. Only just over half of the Microsoft capacity is now planned for delivery by the end of the year, with the rest coming in Q2 2027. The delay is because DataOne, the third-party operator of the site, “decided to wind down the temporary generation faster than it was expected,” according to Andrey Korolenko, chief product and infrastructure officer, as the site switches over to Bloom Energy fuel cells. Still, that transition wasn’t entirely by choice. items.fullText: NVIDIA Expands Open Source Commitment With OpenShell Contribution and New AI Infrastructure At KubeCon, NVIDIA is putting tools to secure agents and run AI on Kubernetes in the hands of the cloud-native community. November 10, 2026 by Warren Barkley 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Kubernetes, the open source system that manages how applications run across thousands of AI factories, has become the foundation for AI, and the demands on it are only growing. To help meet them, NVIDIA is deepening its commitment to open source at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon , the flagship conference for the Kubernetes and cloud-native communities. NVIDIA is contributing NVIDIA OpenShell , an open source runtime for securing and governing autonomous agents, to the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF), a nonprofit that is part of the Linux Foundation and the host of KubeCon. As a CNCF Sandbox project, OpenShell will be governed by the organizations building it into their products and strengthened by the expertise of security professionals worldwide. NVIDIA is also contributing to Agent Substrate , an open source Google-led framework for operating long-running agent workloads at scale on Kubernetes that has been accepted into the CNCF Sandbox. Additionally, NVIDIA announced new components of the NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform : NVIDIA Kubernetes Engine , NVIDIA Kubernetes Recipes and NVIDIA Snapshot . These tools help teams deploy, manage and scale GPU infrastructure on Kubernetes for AI factories. Together, these advancements mark a step forward in making Kubernetes the leading foundation for AI workloads at scale — empowering developers to build safer, more efficient AI infrastructure for the future. items.fullText: NVIDIA Announces New Planned Investments in Korean Startups at the MSIT-NVIDIA AI Startup Partnership Forum November 9, 2026 by NVIDIA Writers 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Korea’s Ministry of Science and ICT and NVIDIA hosted the MSIT -NVIDIA AI Startup Partnership Forum at COEX. Representatives from the Ministry of Science and ICT and NVIDIA met with over 20 Korean startups across foundation models, physical AI, AI infrastructure and AI semiconductors. NVIDIA also announced an investment in Korean startup Point2 , with additional investments planned in Motif Technologies , RLWRLD and Upstage. Point2 Technology, an AI interconnect company, builds scalable, radio frequency-based interconnects that move data between chips and racks in AI factories, offering an innovative alternative to conventional copper and optical interconnect solutions for AI cluster scale-up, delivering the reach, performance and efficiency needed for next-generation AI infrastructure. Motif Technologies , a Seoul-based AI lab, develops foundation models for building AI agents that carry out complex tasks, including Motif-3, a large language model released with open weights. RLWRLD, a physical AI startup based in San Francisco, Seoul and Tokyo, develops robotics foundation models that enable humanoid and industrial robots to perform complex real-world tasks that require five-finger dexterity, such as precisely inserting components, threading nuts onto bolts and kitting parts from moving conveyors. Upstage , a Korean enterprise AI company, develops Solar language models and document AI tools that help businesses extract information from complex documents, streamline workflows and build AI applications for everyday operations. The companies represent work across the full AI stack , from infrastructure to models to robotics applications. items.fullText: From Chips to Skills, NVIDIA and Korea Expand Sovereign AI Collaboration November 8, 2026 by Jesse Clayton 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! NVIDIA and Korea’s Ministry of Science and ICT (MSIT) are expanding their collaboration across the country’s sovereign AI ecosystem, from AI semiconductors and data center infrastructure to talent, startups, models, agents and security. The collaboration lays the groundwork for Korean NPU and XPU companies to explore participation in the NVIDIA NVLink Fusion ecosystem, and includes NVIDIA training and certification programs, hackathons and technical seminars to strengthen GPU utilization. Through Korea’s AI for All initiative, NVIDIA will collaborate with three selected consortia and four leading Korean foundation model builders, using NVIDIA Dynamo software to optimize and scale AI inference. In addition, NVIDIA today announced a collaboration with SK Telecom and Rebellions, supported by MSIT, to advance sovereign AI infrastructure for Korean models and workloads with NVIDIA NVLink Fusion.
